afterburner.settings.title: Afterburner
afterburner.settings.restart: Restart the game to apply the changes
afterburner.settings.forced: Set by a launch option (%s), which this button can't change.
afterburner.settings.server: Works in singleplayer, and on servers that have Afterburner (players don't need it).
afterburner.option.parallelWorldgen.tool: New chunks are generated on every CPU core instead of one, so new land appears faster.
afterburner.option.faceCulling.tooltip: Block faces pointing away from you aren't drawn.
afterburner.option.translucentCulling.to: Water, glass and ice faces pointing away from you aren't drawn.
afterburner.option.leafCulling.tooltip:
Leaf faces deep inside trees aren't drawn: the leaves in front hide them. With see-through leaves (the default), the game otherwise draws every face inside a tree.

The edges of trees look the same; looking into a canopy at a slant shows slightly less inside it.
afterburner.option.drawPrep.tooltip: Skips the work done every frame for chunk layers that have nothing in them.
afterburner.option.chunkBatching.tooltip: Draws many chunks with one call instead of one call per chunk. Most of the rendering options need this.
afterburner.option.compactVertices.toolt: Chunk shapes take less memory, so the graphics card has less to read.
afterburner.option.offscreenBuilds.toolt: Chunks behind you are built while the game has time, so turning around doesn't show missing chunks.
afterburner.option.occlusionCulling.tool: Chunks hidden behind hills and walls aren't drawn. The biggest FPS gain on the ground. A chunk coming into view can rarely show up a frame late.
afterburner.option.entityCulling.tooltip: Mobs, chests, signs and the like hidden behind terrain aren't drawn.
afterburner.option.fastFiltering.tooltip: Smooth texture filtering reads each texture fewer times, for the same picture.
afterburner.option.visibleAnimations.too: Animated textures like water, lava and fire only update while something on screen shows them. Smoother with big resource packs.
afterburner.option.fastBiomeBlend.toolti: Water, grass and leaf colours blend between nearby biomes. While a chunk is being built, each spot's biome is looked up once instead of up to 25 times. Chunks build faster, most of all over oceans. Same colours as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastVisibility.toolti: While you move, the game keeps working out which chunks you can see. Far away, it checks a line from each chunk's corner to you, and it checks most lines several times. This remembers each line's answer while working it out. Same chunks shown as vanilla, worked out faster.
afterburner.option.smoothLightCache.tool: Smooth lighting reads the light around every block face. While a chunk is being built, vanilla remembers only the last 100 blocks it read, so it reads most of them again and again. This remembers every block of the chunk section being built. Chunks build faster. Same lighting as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fpsTarget.tooltip: For slow computers. While the game runs below this, it lowers one thing at a time, what costs the most for the least seen first: clouds, then how far chunks are drawn (the fog comes nearer). When there's room again, they come back. Your own settings aren't changed, and the resolution is never lowered. Off: nothing is lowered.
afterburner.option.fastLight.tooltip: Light updates do less repeated work. The light comes out the same as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastCollisions.toolti: Mobs and players work out what they bump into with less work, and so do items, XP orbs and arrows checking for room every tick. Same results as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastChunkTicks.toolti: Every tick the game looked at every part of every nearby chunk to see if anything in it grows or spreads (grass, crops, leaves, ice), though only a few parts have any. Now it skips the empty parts without looking at them. Same results as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastEntitySearch.tool: Every time something looks for entities near it (mobs pushing each other, items, hoppers, mobs looking for targets), the game went through every entity area along a whole strip of the world. Now it looks only at the few areas near it. Same results as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastMobAi.tooltip: Mob brains and their searches for beds, job blocks and the like take less work. Same results as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastHoppers.tooltip: A hopper with no chest above it looks for a minecart with a chest there every tick, and went through every mob near it to find one. Now it skips the areas that have no minecarts. Same results as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastSpawning.tooltip: Each time the game tries to spawn a group of mobs it looked up which mobs may spawn at the spot, then looked it up again right away,, and looked up the biome there only to check for fish. Every tick it also looked up each mob's spawn cost, which no Overworld or End biome has. Now it looks once, and skips costs where no biome has any. Same results as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastStructures.toolti: Villages, trial chambers, ancient cities and bastions are laid out piece by piece, and each new piece is checked against the room the earlier ones left. Vanilla keeps that room as a shape that gets more complex with every piece; this keeps a list of the pieces' boxes instead. Same structures as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastOres.tooltip: Ore veins asked the world for its height twice for every block they placed. Now they ask once per vein, and copper and iron veins share the noise they both work out for the whole chunk. Same ores as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastBiomeSearch.toolt: New land looks up which biome goes where many times per chunk, in a search tree of thousands of biome entries. This keeps the same tree in flat arrays and stops measuring an entry as soon as it can't be the closest. Same biomes as vanilla.
afterburner.option.fastMobTicks.tooltip: Small checks every mob makes every tick (frost slowdown, rain putting out fire, which goals it may run, how far it's sent to players) take less work. Same results as vanilla.
afterburner.option.parkedTicks.tooltip: Chunks outside simulation distance with water, lava or redstone updates waiting aren't asked again every tick whether they can run them. Same results as vanilla.
afterburner.option.chunkBuffers.tooltip: Graphics memory for chunks grows as needed instead of 128 MB at a time.
afterburner.option.buildCopies.tooltip: Built chunks let go of the copy of blocks they were built from (about 300 MB less at render distance 32).
afterburner.option.memoryTrim.tooltip: While the game is paused or in the background, memory it isn't using goes back to the system.
afterburner.option.workerPriority.toolti: Background work (world generation, chunk building) runs just below normal priority, so frames come first when the CPU is busy.
